approved: Defence Trade Controls Amendment (Genocide, War Crimes and Crimes Against Humanity) Bill 2024
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would stop Australian-made defence goods, technologies and services from being exported if they could be used in genocide or similar serious international crimes.
It would ban exports to a foreign country when the International Court of Justice has ruled that country poses a real and imminent risk of harming a people's right to be protected from genocide.
The bill would also apply when Australia knows or should know of a serious risk of genocide, including after a provisional measures order from the International Court of Justice.
Prohibits exporting Australian defence goods, technologies or services that risk being used in genocide, crimes against humanity or war crimes.
Bans exports to a foreign country that the International Court of Justice has found poses a real and imminent threat of irreparable harm to a people's right to be protected from genocide.
Requires Australia to act with due diligence to ensure its defence exports do not contribute to genocide after they leave the country.
Exporters of Australian-made defence goods, technologies and services.
